title: On Whispering the answer into her ear
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：whisper　|　正文 351 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 whisper 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 the grandmother ① whispered the answer into her ear year after year, and every child in the courtyard said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the grandmother ② whispers the answer into her ear for the whole place without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ whisper the answer into her ear at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ whispered the answer into her ear before — a line in the diary for February 1952 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Whispering the answer into her ear year after year, the grandmother said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the lamp at the far window, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ whisper through the reeds at night for the whole place, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Whisper through the reeds at night at once and never mention it again.

By 1965 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the diary, and a new child from the next courtyard ⑧ whispers through the reeds at night year after year every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the window, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ whispered the answer into her ear again when nobody else would.

⑩ To whisper the answer into her ear, my mother said in 1970, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the courtyard remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the courtyard forgets, somebody whispers the answer into her ear for the whole place again and somebody must whisper the answer into her ear year after year all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 低语（一般过去式 whispered the answer into her ear：1958 年祖母头一回这样做，年年地）
B. v. 低语（一般现在 whispers the answer into her ear：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 低语（不定式 to whisper the answer into her ear：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 低语（过去完成时 had whispered the answer into her ear：1952 年二月的日记上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 低语（动名词 whispering the answer into her ear 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 沙沙作响（whisper through the reeds at night：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去沙沙作响夜间在芦苇间沙沙作响）
G. v. 沙沙作响（whisper through the reeds at night：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 低语（后段两处：新来的孩子照例 whispers through the reeds at night，而母亲又一次 whispered the answer into her ear）

answers.why: whisper 意为“低语”，1958 年祖母年年地低语把答案凑到她耳边低声说，那是院子里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 whispered。
whisper 意为“低语”，自那以后祖母替所有人把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 whispers。
whisper 意为“低语”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯低语把答案凑到她耳边低声说”，此处为不定式 to whisper the answer into her ear。
whisper 意为“低语”，日记里 二月 那行字说明早在 1965 年之前就有人低语过，故用过去完成时 had whispered。
whisper 意为“低语”，祖母说“低语把答案凑到她耳边低声说这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 whispering the answer into her ear 作主语。
whisper 意为“沙沙作响”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去沙沙作响夜间在芦苇间沙沙作响”，should ever 之后用原形 whisper through the reeds at night。
whisper 意为“沙沙作响”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻沙沙作响夜间在芦苇间沙沙作响（whisper through the reeds at night at once），以后再也不要提起。
whisper 意为“低语”，新来的孩子每个年头都照例沙沙作响夜间在芦苇间沙沙作响，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 whispers。
whisper 意为“低语”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次年年地低语把答案凑到她耳边低声说，用一般过去式 whispered 叙述。
whisper 意为“低语”，结尾那句是母亲 1970 年的话：要低语把答案凑到她耳边低声说，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和院子记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 whisper 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1958 the grandmother whispered the answer into her ear year after year, and nobody in the courtyard forgot it.
Even now the grandmother whispers the answer into her ear for the whole place whenever the courtyard asks.
Whispering the answer into her ear year after year, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever whisper through the reeds at night for the whole place, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new child from the next courtyard whispers through the reeds at night year after year every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother whispered the answer into her ear again, and the courtyard remembered that half.
